name: Aurelia House
headline: A better stay starts behind the scenes.
description: A hotel website and operations concept connecting reservations, guest services and room readiness.
alt: Aurelia House hospitality concept artwork with an architectural hotel setting
challenge: Reception needs more than a booking calendar. Room readiness, unpaid balances and guest requests all affect whether the next stay can begin smoothly.
research: The concept maps the guest and reception journeys against the same reservation. This is a workflow exploration, not documented interviews with a hotel client.
goals: Keep guest requests and balances beside the stay
architecture: A browser interface sends reservation and operational actions to a Cloudflare Worker. D1 persists sample records within a separate viewer workspace.
ux: The room, reservation and balance remain visible together. Status labels use text as well as color, and checkout follows the outstanding-balance rules.
ui: Warm hospitality imagery introduces the guest experience; compact tables and room-status cards support reception work.
steps: Choose a stay
Select a room and valid dates. Conflicting sample reservations are rejected.
Manage the guest
Add breakfast or pickup and record a simulated payment beside the reservation.
Complete the stay
Check in, settle the balance, check out and mark the room ready after cleaning.
exercise: Reserve room 202, record a sample payment, check in, check out, then complete housekeeping.
tests: The hosted sample was covered by the previous demo regression suite for reservation rules, workflow actions, persistence and viewer isolation. This Next.js release links to that separate sample.
limits: No live room inventory, OTA connection, payment gateway, transport provider or staff authentication. It is not a production hotel system.
lesson: A room being unoccupied is not the same as a room being ready. Modeling the handoff makes that difference visible.
next: Validate the workflow with reception staff, then scope authentication, live inventory and operational audit logs.
metrics: Booking completion, unpaid balances and time from checkout to room ready.

name: Umar Clinic
headline: Less desk work. More room for care.
description: A reception workflow concept for returning patients, visit queues, payment records and printable slips.
alt: Umar Clinic reception software concept artwork
stack: Original: PHP · SQLite / Hosted sample: JavaScript · D1
challenge: Returning patients, today’s queue and payment reconciliation need to stay connected without staff repeatedly creating the same record.
research: The workflow separates a stable patient record from each visit and payment. It is a reception prototype, not clinical research or an evaluated medical product.
goals: Link repeat visits to a stable sample patient ID
Keep waiting and completed visits distinct
Record payments and refunds without losing their history
architecture: The original local application uses PHP and SQLite. The separate hosted browser sample uses a Worker API and D1 to demonstrate selected reception workflows.
ux: Patient lookup comes before visit creation. Queue status and payment status remain separate so staff can see both without guessing.
ui: Quiet teal accents, clear table headings and compact summaries keep the daily queue readable. Printable slips focus on the current sample visit.
steps: Find the patient
Choose an existing fictional record or register a new sample patient.
Add the visit
Set the sample fee and add the visit to today’s queue.
Close the loop
Mark the visit complete, record payment or refund and print its sample slip.
exercise: Add a fictional patient, create a visit, record payment and print a sample slip.
tests: The previous hosted-demo regression suite covered record creation, visit actions, payment rules and isolated sample workspaces. Public hosting of the original PHP application has not been certified.
limits: Use fictional names only. No diagnoses, real patient data, clinical decisions or production access controls belong in this public sample. It is not an electronic health record.
lesson: Visit status and payment status solve different questions; combining them hides work reception still needs to do.
next: Review data access, retention, backups, permissions and deployment security before considering a real clinic installation.
metrics: Reception entry time, queue clarity and reconciliation of unpaid sample fees.

name: Café Order Workflow
headline: From a conversation to a clear order.
description: An ordering and staff-queue prototype with exact menu totals, explicit confirmation and approval rules.
alt: Café ordering concept artwork with a warm hospitality visual identity
stack: Original: Node.js · Ollama · Whisper / Hosted sample: JavaScript · D1
challenge: Orders arriving in chat are often incomplete. Staff need confirmed items, quantities and delivery details before preparation begins.
research: The prototype breaks ordering into menu selection, review, confirmation and preparation. The rules are explored with sample orders rather than reported client sales data.
goals: Use exact menu prices and quantities
Require confirmation before an order enters the queue
Send oversized orders to staff approval
architecture: The hosted browser demo uses a deterministic menu and server-calculated totals with D1 persistence. The separate original WhatsApp Web prototype explored local AI and transcription.
ux: An order review step separates discussion from commitment. Staff see a preparation queue instead of reconstructing an order from a long conversation.
ui: Warm café imagery, a simple order summary and explicit status controls connect the customer view with preparation work.
steps: Build an order
Choose items and quantities. The server calculates the sample total and delivery.
Confirm once
Review the order; orders above 50 items require staff approval.
Follow preparation
Move the sample order from received to preparing, ready and completed.
exercise: Add two espresso, confirm the order and move it through the staff queue.
tests: The previous hosted-demo regression suite exercised menu totals, order validation and status changes. AI, WhatsApp and transcription integrations are not active in the public browser sample.
limits: The demo does not send WhatsApp messages, call AI or transcribe voice. Original item matching, Urdu parsing, cancellation and reliable staff delivery still need work.
lesson: A model should not invent prices or skip confirmation. Deterministic ordering rules are the foundation for a safer assistant.
next: Repair the original parser, evaluate an official messaging integration and test human handoff before any public bot launch.
metrics: Order correction rate, time to confirmation and preparation handoff time.

name: SportsHub
headline: A place to play, connect and shop.
description: A sports platform concept pairing event participation with a simple catalog, basket and sample checkout.
alt: SportsHub sports and commerce concept artwork
stack: Original: PHP · MySQL / Hosted sample: JavaScript · D1
challenge: Players need to discover sessions and participate easily, while store operators need clear orders and reliable availability.
research: The concept follows event discovery and shopping as separate journeys with shared navigation. No community growth or sales lift has been measured.
goals: Make joining and leaving an event clear
Show basket quantities and totals before confirmation
Validate sample stock before recording an order
architecture: The original platform uses PHP and MySQL. The hosted sample independently demonstrates events, basket actions and inventory-aware sample orders through a Worker and D1.
ux: Events and commerce have clear entry points. A sample order reference closes the checkout flow, while stock validation prevents an unavailable purchase.
ui: Sport-led imagery introduces the community; product cards, totals and readable action states keep the commerce flow practical.
steps: Find a session
Explore sample events and join or leave in your viewer workspace.
Build a basket
Add available products, change quantities and review the total.
Place a sample order
Confirm a simulated checkout, receive a reference and see stock update.
exercise: Join an event, add a football to your basket and place a sample order.
tests: The previous hosted-demo regression suite covered event participation, baskets, stock validation and order persistence. Full runtime and security testing of the original PHP platform remains outstanding.
limits: No real payments, shipping, event admission or community messaging. The original PHP checkout binding defect and administrative request protection require fixes before release.
lesson: Participation and purchasing share an audience but have different failure cases. Each needs its own clear completion state.
next: Resolve original checkout and administrative security defects, then validate authorization and real payment-provider behavior in staging.
metrics: Event participation, basket completion and stock accuracy.
